recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-32824 unless PA opens a new issue to add an explicit unknown status code or make Endpoint.status optional despite the published R5 resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-32824 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for Endpoint.status. The reporter asked for either an unknown status code or 0..1 cardinality because endpoint directories may not know the current health/status of an endpoint. The PA work group instead resolved to clarify Endpoint.status and Endpoint.period usage, leaving status mandatory and without an unknown code.
initial_application: Commit ed05f6312aaa6fdf04780c93f1b9baa2d927b4ed applied FHIR-32824 by changing Endpoint.status to a general expected availability definition, adding the temporary-downtime comment to Endpoint.status, and adding the corresponding Endpoint.period comment in source/endpoint/structuredefinition-Endpoint.xml.
additional_context: Endpoint is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. Later Applied/Persuasive with Modification issue FHIR-36017 explicitly revised Endpoint.status wording, added Endpoint.availability for specific availability including transient downtimes and exceptions, and clarified Endpoint.period's planned lifecycle purpose. The combined branch already contains the FHIR-36017 reconciliation commit 504023192d19571d31acb27dc45aa4c14f9c7365. PA minutes confirm FHIR-32824's persuasive-with-modification vote, and targeted Zulip searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source keeps Endpoint.status 1..1, does not add an unknown Endpoint status code, retains the short-term downtime clarification, and now uses Endpoint.availability for the more specific transient availability details introduced by FHIR-36017.
